label: Daniel K. Inouye
narrative: Inouye is the reason the money moved without a floor fight. As chairman of the Senate Appropriations Committee (and previously chair of Defense Appropriations) he controlled the vehicle through which discretionary defense spending is written, and his agreement let Reid and Ted Stevens route roughly $22 million into the classified annex of the FY2008 defense appropriation rather than into a line item anyone would have to defend publicly. The mechanism matters more than the man: an appropriation placed in the black budget by three senators, two of them the ranking figures of the appropriations process, is not subject to the authorizing committees' scrutiny and does not appear in any public budget justification. That is the precise structural gap the modern disclosure fight is about. Inouye had a decades-long record of pushing back on intelligence-community secrecy from inside the process — he co-chaired the Iran-Contra committee — which makes his participation here a deliberate act rather than a favour. He died in office on 17 December 2012, the same year AAWSAP/AATIP was terminated.
